status: design-only; runtime coordinates, navigation and NPC bindings are not yet surveyed
designIntent: A large coastal district that feels like a genuine extension of Hyland Point, not a small isolated outpost.

zones.name: Harbor Gate and Customs Approach
zones.purpose: Main road connection, port administration, vehicle queue and access control.

zones.name: Container Port and Shipyard
zones.purpose: Container stacks, cranes, loading lanes, quay, repair sheds, shipyard and freight handling.

zones.name: Freight and Logistics Park
zones.purpose: Large warehouses, cold storage, loading docks, truck staging, freight depot and delivery offices.

zones.name: Harbor Market and High Street
zones.purpose: Market hall, walkable main street, shops, restaurants, service businesses and a central public square.

zones.name: Industrial and Vehicle Service Quarter
zones.purpose: Vehicle workshop, industrial maintenance, power infrastructure, fabrication and service yards.

zones.name: Workers' Residential Quarter
zones.purpose: Apartment blocks, worker housing, local diner, laundromat, convenience store and small parking courts.

zones.name: Waterfront, Marina and Pier Promenade
zones.purpose: Public waterfront, fishing spots, marina, small boat dock, seafood café, bait shop and visitor areas.

populationPolicy: All physical NPC IDs are stable and namespaced.
The first in-game vertical slice remains 3-5 NPCs; scale toward 42 only after pathfinding, save/load, multiplayer and performance tests pass.
Do not instantiate all 42 at once unless the target game build proves that scene streaming and NPC scheduling can handle it.
Police officers are not included in this roster; they are owned and spawned by the native law-enforcement system.

existingBusinessSystems: native shop catalogue and cash/inventory systems
businessAndServices.rule: Candidate listings are not enabled until the existing Realtor registration and purchase lifecycle is proven in-game.

police.system: Schedule I native LawController, LawManager and CheckpointManager
police.activationPolicy: Use discovered native police routes and the existing global law intensity/automatic evaluation rules. Do not force-spawn officers or change the global heat level to fake local police activity.
police.localPoliceFacilityImplementation: Reuse the native vanilla police-station prefab and verify its station registration/officer pool in the live scene

drugPreferences.runtimeCatalog: S1API.Products.DrugType enum enumerated from the installed runtime
drugPreferences.assignmentAlgorithm: save-seeded deterministic per-NPC affinity vectors with uniqueness enforced within the Harborline customer roster
drugPreferences.assignmentTiming: once when the host initializes a new world/save roster, then persisted and synchronized
notes: Do not use the expansion-only sime.product.batch.* order tiers as DrugType affinities.
Do not hardcode DrugType names that are absent from the installed game.
If the installed runtime exposes too few DrugType combinations for all unique profiles, fail validation rather than silently cloning preferences.
drugPreferences.nativeApplication: Pass mapped (DrugType, affinity) tuples to the native NPCCustomer builder's WithAffinities inside WithCustomerDefaults

appearance.system: S1API NPCAppearance typed customization builder with deterministic seeded profile selection
appearance.randomizationTiming: once per NPC identity, not on every schedule tick
required: Call NPCAppearance.GenerateRandomAppearance() in the native OnCreated lifecycle.
Apply the NPC's deterministic NpcAppearanceProfile using documented native customization fields and layer APIs.
Call Appearance.Build() after the final appearance fields are applied.
Use one stable appearance profile per NPC ID and persist it with the host save; never reroll during update ticks or schedule changes.
Verify all selected native asset paths in the installed game build and compare rendered appearances in-game before release.
appearance.publicApiLimit: S1API exposes native random generation and explicit avatar fields/layers but no documented appearance-signature readback. The mod therefore prevents descriptor collisions within its own roster before applying them; visual collisions against vanilla or other mods must be inspected in-game.
appearance.assignmentAlgorithm: SHA-256 save-seeded, per-NPC unique visual profiles applied with native NPCAppearance.Set, WithFaceLayer, WithBodyLayer and WithAccessoryLayer; do not reroll locally on each peer
appearance.uniquenessScope: All expansion-owned appearance descriptors in the 42-person Harborline roster are unique; comparison against vanilla and third-party NPCs remains an in-game compatibility check
notes: Generate each full appearance profile from the persisted host-owned seed before NPC creation.
Apply the saved profile via the native NPCAppearance typed customization API in OnCreated, then call Build.
Do not call GenerateRandomAppearance independently on every client after a saved deterministic profile exists; that can create host/client visual divergence.
On a missing asset or API error, keep/build the native default avatar and log the failure; do not roll a local random fallback.
Visual comparison with vanilla and third-party NPCs still requires in-game testing.

releaseGates: Capture real world-space anchors, elevations, entrances and road connections in the target game build.
Build a greybox and validate pedestrian/vehicle navigation before enabling full NPC population.
Prove one customer NPC end-to-end using native DrugType affinities, native schedule, save/load and two-player late join.
Prove distinct randomized appearance settings remain stable after save/load and are not duplicated in the generated Harborline roster.
Prove two native police patrol routes and all three checkpoint anchors without altering unrelated vanilla districts.
Prove new property candidates through the original Realtor UI and native purchase lifecycle.
Record host/client performance at 5, 10, 16 and 20 simultaneously active NPCs.
Apply all 42 unique appearance profiles through the live S1API avatar wrapper and verify the selected asset paths render correctly.
Compare active Harborline appearance results against visible vanilla NPCs and other installed S1API NPC mods where the running API permits inspection.
